records.title: Supported models
records.description: Load one model at a time with aquin load model. Catalog slugs (gpt2-small, gte-small) include curated public SAEs where available. Family support lets you pass a HuggingFace repo id for other sizes in the same architectu
records.text:
Load one model at a time with aquin load model. Catalog slugs (gpt2-small, gte-small) include curated public SAEs where available. Family support lets you pass a HuggingFace repo id for other sizes in the same architecture: GPT-2, Pythia, Llama, Qwen, and common embedding encoders. Run aquin list model for the catalog and family examples.
Pass any example HuggingFace id to aquin load model. Aquin introspects layer count and width, then runs the same tool suite as the catalog entry. Public SAE pull (aquin load sae) applies to catalog models; on family models use aquin sae train to build a temporary SAE first.
One model in VRAM at a time. Run aquin load model again to switch.
Catalog: feature tools need a public SAE. Run aquin list sae, then aquin load sae <model-l{n}>.
Family models: train with aquin sae train, then aquin load sae --user <name> before inspect.
Fine-tuned weights stay on disk. Use --checkpoint while the base model id stays loaded.
Page: /docs/models

records.description: The Aquin web dashboard at aquin.app/app: session tabs, CLI inbox, analyst chat, interactive cards, and research attachments.
records.text:
The web dashboard
Aquin web dashboard at aquin.app/app is your analyst workspace
You do not run forward passes here; attach tracked CLI command outputs, inspect interactive cards, and talk to an analyst
Counterpart to the terminal: the CLI does compute locally, the dashboard is where you make sense of it
Everything is organized into session tabs, each with its own analyst chat and attached results

records.title: Sessions and tabs
records.description: Create a session with one click via New session; tabs open instantly and titles are editable or auto-generated.
records.text:
Sessions and tabs on the Aquin dashboard
Create a session with a single click on New session in the sidebar; a new tab opens immediately titled New chat
No naming step to get in the way
Titles are editable: hover a tab and click the pencil to rename it
If you never rename it, the first message you send generates a short descriptive chat title automatically
Renaming yourself always takes priority over the automatic title
Delete a session from the hover controls; it does not touch local command records under ~/.aquin/commands/

records.title: The CLI inbox
records.description: Recent command outputs auto-upload to the inbox; click items to attach one or more to a session chat.
records.text:
The CLI inbox on the Aquin dashboard
Every GPU tool you run writes a local record and, when logged in, auto-uploads it to your inbox
The inbox lives at the bottom of the sidebar and lists recent command outputs across every tool
Disable auto-upload with AQUIN_AUTO_SEND=0 and push manually with aquin commands send <id>
Click any inbox item to attach it to the current session
Attach more than one output to a single chat to reason across inspections, simulations, and evals together
Attached items show as a counter in the chat input; click the counter to open a popover and detach items
Documentation: /docs/agent

records.description: The --output flag was removed. Use --check for JSON+PNG artifacts, --save for custom exports, --dir for captures.
records.text:
CLI flag migration: --output removed
Old: aquin trace --output json
New: aquin trace --check
Old: aquin capture-activations --output ./captures/run
New: aquin activations capture --dir ./captures/run
Old: aquin diff sae --output /tmp/out.json
New: aquin diff sae --save /tmp/out.json
Use --check for machine-readable JSON and PNG files in cwd
Use --save when a command supports writing JSON to a specific path
Use --dir for activations capture output directory
Scripting, automation, CI, parse json from CLI

records.title: Agentic & Basic CLI
records.description: Cross-cutting commands: installation, authentication, aquin status (logged-in account, CLI token, and loaded model state), model loading, local command tracking, CLI inbox upload, the aquin chat agent loop, one-shot basi
records.text:
Agentic & Basic CLI
Cross-cutting commands: installation, authentication, aquin status (logged-in account, CLI token, and loaded model state), model loading, local command tracking, CLI inbox upload, the aquin chat agent loop, one-shot basic CLI invocation, and legacy packaging. These apply regardless of LLM vs embedding mode unless noted. GPU tools run against the model loaded with aquin load model (one model in VRAM at a time; run load again to switch). Tracked command outputs auto-upload to your web CLI inbox when logged in. On aquin.app, open a session tab, attach inbox items to the analyst chat, and inspect interactive result cards in the sidebar. Profile → Account holds your CLI token (generate or regenerate).
Prerequisite: aquin login · aquin load model <model-id> · aquin status
Page: /docs/agent

Section: Agentic & Basic CLI

records.title: aquin load sae
records.description: Download or activate a sparse autoencoder for feature-level tools. Catalog: aquin load sae <model-l{n}> pulls public weights. User-trained: aquin load sae --user <name> [--layer N] after aquin sae train, or --path <file.
records.text:
Section: Agentic & Basic CLI
Command: aquin load sae
Download or activate a sparse autoencoder for feature-level tools. Catalog: aquin load sae <model-l{n}> pulls public weights. User-trained: aquin load sae --user <name> [--layer N] after aquin sae train, or --path <file.pt>. Binding is stored in ~/.aquin/active_user_sae.json.
Flags:
<model-l{n}>: Catalog SAE slug from aquin list sae.
--user: Activate a user-trained SAE by run name (loaded model must match).
--path: Activate from an explicit .pt path.
--layer: SAE layer (required if run has multiple layers).
--model: Model slug when using --path without .meta.json.
CLI flags: <model-l{n}> --user --path --layer --model
Example:
aquin load sae gpt2-small-l8
aquin sae train --layer 8 --name my-run --quick
aquin load sae --user my-run --layer 8
aquin trace --prompt "hello" --layer 8
Documentation: /docs/agent#aquin-load-sae

records.title: aquin compare simulation
records.description: Side-by-side diff of two saved simulation runs. LLM: predicted loss delta, SAE feature shifts, LiSSA influence changes, attack-surface metrics (consistency, suppression, robustness). Embedding: loss trajectory, geometry
records.text:
Section: Agentic & Basic CLI
Command: aquin compare simulation
Agent tool: compare_simulations
Side-by-side diff of two saved simulation runs. LLM: predicted loss delta, SAE feature shifts, LiSSA influence changes, attack-surface metrics (consistency, suppression, robustness). Embedding: loss trajectory, geometry metrics, triplet margin satisfaction. Both runs must be the same kind (LLM vs LLM or embed vs embed).
Flags:
--run_id_a (required): First run (before / baseline).
--run_id_b (required): Second run (after / variant).
--label_a / --label_b: Display labels in the comparison table.
CLI flags: --run_id_a --run_id_b --label_a / --label_b
Example:
aquin compare simulation --run_id_a ae15a72ab0ca --run_id_b 1e39f85fbf6a
Notes: Legacy alias: aquin compare-runs. Typical use: compare two simulate configs (dataset cleanup, LR tweak, rank change). See /docs/simulation/llm or /docs/simulation/embedding.
Documentation: /docs/agent#aquin-compare-simulation

records.description: One-shot basic CLI: any tool verb from the registry (trace, steer, simulate, check layer, etc.) without agent orchestration. Same GPU path as chat. Each run is tracked locally and auto-uploads to your CLI inbox when logg
records.text:
Section: Agentic & Basic CLI
Command: aquin <tool-verb>
One-shot basic CLI: any tool verb from the registry (trace, steer, simulate, check layer, etc.) without agent orchestration. Same GPU path as chat. Each run is tracked locally and auto-uploads to your CLI inbox when logged in. Add --check to save JSON + PNG artifacts for scripting; use --save for a custom JSON export path where supported.
Flags:
--check: Save JSON + PNG check artifacts in cwd.
CLI flags: --check
Example:
aquin trace --prompt "The capital of France is"

records.text:
SAE training
Collect activations from labeled probe sets (LLM resid_post or embedding hidden states) and train temporary sparse autoencoders on checkpoint weights or saved activation shards. Works on catalog models and supported families (GPT-2, Pythia, Llama, Qwen, BERT-style encoders) after aquin load model. Catalog models may use aquin load sae for a public dictionary; family models typically need aquin sae train first. Use aquin activations capture for probe-scale exports; reuse them with sae train --activations or train directly from corpus (writes _acts_layer<N>/ for later reuse). Tracked locally; auto-uploads to your CLI inbox when logged in.
Prerequisite: aquin login · aquin load model llama-3.2-1b

Agent tool: run_capture_activations
Run a batch of probes through the loaded model, capture activations per layer, and write a manifest + tensor shards. Optional --checkpoint patches fine-tuned weights (LLM .pt or embedding .pt / HF directory).

--prompts: Optional JSON/JSONL probes. Omit to auto-generate with --count and --topic.
--count: Number of probes when auto-generating (default: 6, max: 64).
--topic: Theme for generated probes (default: general knowledge…).
--layers: Comma-separated layer indices or all (default: all).
--checkpoint: Fine-tuned checkpoint (.pt state dict or HF directory; omit for base model).
--position: Pool tokens: last (default) or mean.
--granularity: prompt (default) or token. Token mode writes token_spans.jsonl.
--balance: Balance probes evenly across metadata groups.
--group: Metadata field used with --balance (optional).
--encode-sae: Also write SAE feature vectors for --sae-layer (requires pulled public SAE).
--sae-layer: Layer for --encode-sae (default: model SAE layer).
--name: Capture label in manifest (default: checkpoint stem or base).
--check: Save capture-activations-check.json and capture-activations-check.png in cwd.
CLI flags: --dir --prompts --count --topic --layers --checkpoint --position --granularity --balance --group --encode-sae --sae-layer --name --check
Example:
aquin load model llama-3.2-1b

aquin activations capture --count 8 --topic "factual reasoning" \
  --layers 8 --dir ./captures/my-run --balance

aquin activations capture --prompts ~/Aquin/fixtures/e2e/llm/capture_probes.jsonl \

aquin activations capture --prompts probes.jsonl \
  --layers 8 --dir ./captures/tokens --granularity token

records.text:
Section: SAE training
Command: aquin sae train
Agent tool: run_sae_train
Train a temporary SAE on activations streamed from a corpus, checkpoint weights, or a saved activation directory. LLMs use TransformerLens resid_post; embedding models use mean-pooled hidden states. Use --quick for smoke tests. Output: ~/.aquin/sae/user/<model>/… or ~/.aquin/sae/user/embed-<model>/…
Flags:
--model (required): Loaded model slug or family HuggingFace id (must match aquin load model).
--layer (required): Hook layer index.
--checkpoint: Fine-tuned checkpoint .pt (omit for base-model SAE).
--activations: Reuse saved activations: _acts_layer<N> from a prior train, chunk_*.pt dir, or activations capture output (manifest + layers/). Skips forward passes.
--balance: When training from a capture dir, import a balanced subset of probes first.
--group: Metadata field used with --balance (optional).
--quick: Shorter training run (~100k tokens).
--corpus: JSON/JSONL text corpus (default: streamed OpenWebText). Ignored with --activations.
--name: Tag for output directory under ~/.aquin/sae/user/.
--save: Explicit output .pt path.
CLI flags: --model --layer --checkpoint --activations --balance --group --quick --corpus --name --save
Example:
aquin load model gpt2-medium

aquin sae train --layer 8 --quick --name my-run

aquin activations capture --layers 8 --dir ./captures/my-run --encode-sae
aquin sae train --layer 8 --activations ./captures/my-run --name probe-sae --quick --balance --group label

records.title: aquin feature locate
records.description: Generate completions from deception probes (default), classify each response against honest/deceptive references, bucket by observed behavior, encode prompt+completion with the public SAE, and rank features by mean activ
records.text:
Section: Deception feature identification
Command: aquin feature locate
Agent tool: run_find_feature
Generate completions from deception probes (default), classify each response against honest/deceptive references, bucket by observed behavior, encode prompt+completion with the public SAE, and rank features by mean activation delta (deceptive − honest). Use --conditioning prompt for legacy static probe-text encoding. LLMs use token-mean residual activations; embedding models use mean-pooled hidden states (prompt conditioning only). Use --direction to filter by sign: both (|Δ|, default), deceptive (Δ>0), honest (Δ<0). Optionally re-rank top candidates with InterpScore (--benchmark-top) and persist the chosen index (--persist).
Flags:
--scorer: Scorer name (default: deception).
--prompts: JSON/JSONL probe file with prompt + honest_reference + deceptive_reference (or paired honest/deceptive rows). Omit to use bundled fixtures/deception/deception_probes.jsonl.
--layer: SAE layer (default: model default from load sae).
--checkpoint: Optional fine-tuned checkpoint (.pt state dict or HF directory).
--top: Number of ranked features to return (default 20).
--direction: both (|Δ|, default), deceptive (Δ>0 only), or honest (Δ<0 only).
--conditioning: behavior (default): generate + classify output; prompt: static probe text only.
--benchmark-top: Re-rank top K with InterpScore + Purity (needs OpenAI).
--persist: Write chosen feature to ~/.aquin/experiments/<model>.json and session memory.
--save: Write full JSON result to path.
--umap: Load SAE UMAP projection after ranking (web explorer).

aquin feature locate --prompts fixtures/deception/deception_probes.jsonl --layer 8 --direction deceptive --persist deception_feature --umap

records.title: aquin diff weight
records.description: Per-layer weight delta between the catalog base model and a fine-tuned checkpoint, plus rank/collapse signals, merge verdict (pass | warn | fail), and optional behavioral model-diff on probe generations (LLM only). LLMs
records.text:
Section: Checkpoint diff & SAE analysis
Command: aquin diff weight
Agent tool: run_merge_analysis
Per-layer weight delta between the catalog base model and a fine-tuned checkpoint, plus rank/collapse signals, merge verdict (pass | warn | fail), and optional behavioral model-diff on probe generations (LLM only). LLMs report Q/K/V/O/MLP ‖ΔW‖ and stable rank (full weights via TransformerLens, or LoRA effective B@A). Embedding models diff HF encoder weights grouped by layer. Exit code 2 on fail. Tracks a mergeAnalysis card and uploads to your CLI inbox when logged in.
Flags:
--checkpoint (required): Path to merged .pt checkpoint or HF save_pretrained directory.
--name: Label for checkpoint in output and inbox card (default: filename stem).
--prompts: JSON array or JSONL probes for behavioral diff (LLM).

aquin diff weight --checkpoint ~/Aquin/fixtures/e2e/.work/aquin_run/checkpoints/checkpoint.pt \

records.title: aquin diff sae
records.description: Load the catalog base model and a fine-tuned checkpoint, run the same prompts through the public SAE, and report per-feature activation deltas (changed count, mean/max |Δ|, top features). LLMs use TransformerLens residua
records.text:
Section: Checkpoint diff & SAE analysis
Command: aquin diff sae
Agent tool: run_sae_diff
Load the catalog base model and a fine-tuned checkpoint, run the same prompts through the public SAE, and report per-feature activation deltas (changed count, mean/max |Δ|, top features). LLMs use TransformerLens residuals; embedding models use mean-pooled layer activations. Tracks a saeDiff card and uploads to your CLI inbox when logged in.
Flags:
--checkpoint (required): Path to merged .pt checkpoint or HF save_pretrained directory.
--prompts: JSON array or JSONL of probe strings / {instruction, response} rows.
--layer: SAE layer (default: from model config).
--sae: Custom SAE weights path instead of pulled public SAE.
--name: Label for checkpoint in output and inbox card (default: checkpoint filename).
--save: Write full JSON payload to disk.
CLI flags: --checkpoint --prompts --layer --sae --name --save
Example:
aquin diff sae --checkpoint ~/Aquin/fixtures/e2e/.work/aquin_run/checkpoints/checkpoint.pt \
  --prompts ~/Aquin/fixtures/e2e/llm/sae_diff_prompts.json \
  --name e2e-fixture --save /tmp/sae-diff.json
Notes: Uses the loaded session model. Checkpoint format: { step, state_dict } from run.checkpoint() or fixtures/e2e/scripts/train_lora_e2e.py.
Documentation: /docs/checkpoint-sae#aquin-diff-sae

records.text:
Training watch
Passive observer for external training runs. Not aquin simulate and not checkpoint diff tools. Your trainer (PyTorch loop, custom script, Aquin SDK, etc.) writes metrics as JSONL; aquin watch streams those lines into ~/.aquin/watch/<run_id>/ (manifest.json + events.jsonl). A new run is registered automatically when you pass --file. Aquin does not run optimizer steps or store merged weights here. For post-training checkpoint analysis, see Checkpoint SAE (/docs/checkpoint-sae). Simulation runs stay in ~/.aquin/runs/ and appear under aquin list simulation. Watch does not require a loaded model.
Prerequisite: aquin login (optional; watch runs locally without GPU)
Page: /docs/watch

records.title: aquin watch --file <path>
records.description: Register a watch run (when --run is omitted) and stream metrics from a JSONL file. Batch mode reads the file once and exits. With --follow, keeps tailing the file as new lines are appended during live training.
records.text:
Section: Training watch
Command: aquin watch --file <path>
Register a watch run (when --run is omitted) and stream metrics from a JSONL file. Batch mode reads the file once and exits. With --follow, keeps tailing the file as new lines are appended during live training.
Flags:
--file (required): Path to metrics JSONL.
--follow: Tail the file; ingest new lines as they appear.
--run: Existing watch run id (skip auto-register).
--name: Run label when creating a new watch.
--model: Base model slug shown on charts (e.g. llama-3.2-1b).
--finish: Mark run stopped when streaming ends.
--map src=dst: Rename a metric column (e.g. --map train_loss=loss).
--step-field: Step column name (default: step, global_step, …).
--offset: Skip first N lines (resume).
--auto-step: Assign steps 0,1,2… when rows have no step field.
CLI flags: --file --follow --run --name --model --finish --map src=dst --step-field --offset --auto-step
Example:
aquin watch --file ./metrics.jsonl --follow --model llama-3.2-1b

# Append to an existing run:
aquin watch --run ae15a72ab0ca --file ./metrics.jsonl --follow
Notes: Fixture: fixtures/e2e/watch/metrics.jsonl. One JSON object per line. Scalar keys (loss, learning_rate, grad_norm, epoch) become chart channels. Special rows: {"type":"signal",…} and {"status":"stopped"}.
Documentation: /docs/watch#aquin-watch---file-path
